Report Details

Violation ID: 8271098
Permit API: 051-21425
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On April 13 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445. Accompanying me in today's inspection is Rosie Wise (PaDEP)The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.As previously described in IR 4157445:The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet.Upon inspection of the well posting, it appeared a new well posting has been installed on a piece of the production equipment in accordance with OGA3211(H). The well posting appeared to contain the well permit number, operator's name, and operator's phone number. However, it did not appear to contain the operator's address. The Department recommends the operator ensure all required information is properly posted in accordance with OGA3211(G).Based on today's inspection, OGA3211(H) is being closed. All other violations issued in IR 4157445 remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/12/2024 to FARRINGTON & HEPLER GAS & OIL INC in Washington Township, Jefferson county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: FARRINGTON & HEPLER GAS & OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/12/2024
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8201067
Permit API: 065-26269
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/12/2024
Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Violation ID: 8264949
Permit API: 125-23052
Unconventional: No
County: Washington

Inspection Date: 2/19/2026
Comments: On 02/19/2026, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the SPESAK F41 in Fallowfield Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-The Department found a release and spill of over range fluid leaking from a cracked hose to production tank labeled #1. I observed discolored elevated fluid of 5.89 mS/cm and 6.89 mS/cm throughout the Earthen Berm contaiment. It appears the spill is greater than 42 gallons and the Department recommends following Act 2 remediation guidelines. No rainwater outlet was observed (Photo 1-7).-An unnamed stream was 147 ft downslope of the release. I observed no elevated fluid within stream at the time of inspection (Photo 8 and 9).-Field Scout Conductivity probe was calibrated on 02/18/2026.-The Department contacted Diversified Lisa Raffle at the time of observation. I was contacted by Glen at Diversified stating a well tender was going to come shut-in the well and a truck to remove the fluid as soon as possible. Violations are being issued for: 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), 78.66(b).

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative

Violation Code: 78.121(A) - WELL REPORTING – PRODUCTION REPORTING – Conventional operator failed to submit annual conventional production and status report for permitted or registered well.
Violation ID: 8176099
Permit API: 065-26057
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Henderson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/21/2024
Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in November/December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. As per this administrative order, a written remediation plan was to be submitted to the Department by 5/26/23, and a final remediation report is to be submitted by 12/31/23. No remediation plans have been received by the Department as of this date. A Petition to Enforce was filed in Commonwealth Court on 8/16/2023. In response to that petition, a Commonwealth Order was issued on 12/13/2023 requiring a Remediation Schedule to be submitted to the Department within 60 days. No Remediation Schedule has been received, and a new violation has been issued for failure to comply with the terms of the issued court order.The contractor (Bigler Boyz Environmental) began remediation of this site on 8/17/23. Three roll-off containers remain on-site, and it appears that remediation has been completed. No soil sample documentation has been received by the Department as of this date, and heavy deer tracks at the restored site indicate that there may still be some residual contamination. All documentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/6/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655836), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 12/12/2022, I conducted a follow up inspection of the DR02 Pad and Impoundment ESX 1H well. Nucomer has hired a 3rd party contractor "Assist" to complete the secondary containment liner repair. TJ Pennino from EMKEY Gathering was on site representing Nucomer Energy. This is in response to violations in previous inspections(3459581). The violations are for tears and holes in the secondary containment liner in the tank battery. Two different methods were being utilized in the repair attempt. One is a hot air weld of liner material. The second was a PVC extruder gun as seen in photo #3. It should be noted the original containment liner is thickness of 20 mil. The patch material brought by Assist for the hot air welding is a 40 mil thickness. After several attempts to hot air weld the patch material to the existing liner, it was evident trying to weld the 40 mil patch material to the 20 mil existing material was not going to work. Several pieces of the 20 mil liner were cut from outside containment and cleaned as best as possible. Again the original liner material is too thin and was not supporting a good hot-air weld. The extruder was used on several smaller holes. It became obvious it is not suitable to be used on a material of this thickness. The temperature was set as low as the machine would allow and the material melted through the original liner (pictures #1 and #4).After several attempts trying several different methods, the decision was made by TJ to abandon the repair attempt. TJ was going to speak with ASSIST and plan another course of action and discuss options available.Additionally the violation for the 55 gallon drums being stored outside of secondary containment, can be closed. This violation has been resolved.

Comments: On February 8, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Kiskiminetas Spring School 4 well in Loyalhanna Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3488724, where high conductivity was found underneath the brine tank valve. The Department had yet to receive the waste manifest from remediation or the quantity released in the spill noted in IR 3307023, therefore the Department was unable to assess whether the spill had been remediated in accordance with DEP Spill Policy. Violations were continued as a result, and the Department requested that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information no later than February 10, 2023. Heavy tire rutting was also observed on the access road. Present were myself, DEP OGI Curtis Small, Brian Haney from PA Mineral Services, and Joe Miller from Mid Atlantic Energy Services. The following was observed:The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photo 7). The API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 4). This information now reflects the information that the Department has on file. A hissing sound and a strong gas odor was observed coming from the well head at the time of inspection (see photo 5). Mr. Haney and Mr. Miller were making repairs on the well head at the time of inspection. The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 3). However, elevated conductivity remains underneath the brine tank valve (see photo 1). A background soil conductivity reading was taken along the access road, which read 120 Microsiemens (see photo 9). Heavy tire rutting remains in the access road (see photo 8). It was initially noted that the access road is shared with the operator and Kiski Prep School. However, Mr. Haney informed the Department that unrelated timber trucks also use the access road for removal of trees for timber. Trees that are said to be marked for timber use could be observed north of the well site (see photo 6).Based on observations from this inspection, the the Department recommends that the operator investigate the cause of the elevated conductivity and remediate accordingly. Violations remain outstanding. The Department also recommends that the operator cooperatively monitor and maintain the access road with Kiski School, and Timber companies that use it to prevent accelerated erosion. The Department requests that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information, including quantity released no later than February 10, 2023.

Inspection Date: 11/30/2022
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's OMR 02-188 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 11/30/2022 at 0920 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with an overcast, light rain and moderate winds. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced water reported by the operator. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID #368537 is tied to this release within CTSOn 11/29/2022 Repsol reported a 42 gallon release of produced water to the ground surface at the OMR 02-188 well site after a produced water flow-line was cut during the teardown process. Some produced water was initially pumped out of the line but not all was recovered prior to the cut of the flow-line. The produced water was then released to the ground in numerous areas along the flow-line. The impacted areas were then covered with tarps to help keep the areas free from the projected rain prior to excavation/remediation.During today's inspection, the impacted areas remained covered with tarps and a secondary containment liner to help prevent rain from spreading the release. Water present in the rock-lined channel located below the release area was field measured for electrical conductivity between 200us/cm to 380us/cm. Pad material and soils around the impacted areas covered by tarps were field measured for electrical conductivity between 0.1mS/cm and 0.3mS/cm. No evidence suggests that the release was able to reach the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls.The operator was awaiting an 811 call approval and for the environmental consultant to arrive in order to begin remediation. Current estimations put an excavation start time at 1300 hours on 11/30/2022. Discussion with an operator representative onsite places the release estimate at ~42 gallons, or one barrel, but it is not exactly known. Current rainfall would have a chance to commingle with the release prior to total recovery. Photos of the initial release discovery were provided to me via email. The operator explained that Act 2 sampling was planned to be conducted.Based on the reported release of 42 gallons of produced water to the ground, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22132 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1020 hours.

The majority of the areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover. Areas disturbed during the construction of the new access road loop remain temporarily stabilized with erosion control blanket/straw. The area holding the fluids with elevated EC are shown in photos #6 and 8. Due to the elevated EC field readings, a sample for standard analysis code 942 was collected (sample ID #0983-405) from the puddle shown in photos # 9 and 10. Comments: On September 23, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo Resource's Whyel 1 Well located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following violations issued under inspection report 3875658. IR 4055015 documents an Operator response the Department received which states: "Apollo Resources LLC is responding to an inspection report on Wyhel Well 37-051-23812. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding pending the receipt of the aforementioned documents.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 10/13/2022
Violation Code: 78a64a(h) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Inspection reports and maintenance records failed to be available at the well site for review by the Department.
Violation ID: 972779
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Comments: On 11/16/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. This inspection is in response to Complaint Id 368309 for one barrel of brine water spilled outside of secondary containment from a frac tank on the site.Prior to my arrival, Chesapeake's Danielle Schaad informed me that the frac tank would be to the right when arriving on site and was stationed in secondary containment by itself. She said that the location of the leak in the frac tank and in the secondary containment was unknown but high conductance water was discovered outside of secondary containment on the pad surface. She said that the fluid was brine water from the produced water tank. She reported that the tank and secondary containment had been emptied and the puddle vacuumed up. She said that the tank was being removed from location and that Cresson Environmental would be onsite on 11/17/2022. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours and was melting with the pad being mostly clear of snow. A skid steer and a vac truck had just arrived on location and were setting up next to a frac tank in the northeast corner of the site. The frac tank was still connected to the 1HC gas well GPU. A crew was working on disconnecting it from the GPU. A vac box was located south of the frac tank. I field tested various water puddles in close proximity to the frac tank for conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50 with an upper limit of 20.0 mS with the following results: 40'x 40' water puddle on the south west corner of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 0.77 mS.5' x 8' water puddle outside the southeast corner of the vac box field tested at 14.43 mS.20' x 20' water puddle southeast of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.15 x 30' water puddle east of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.6' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 3.53 mS.12' x 40' water puddle on the east edge of the site above the recently excavated fill slope field tested at 2.33 mS.Water below the rocked section of the fill slope field tested at 1.20 mS. Water in the south end of infiltration area 1 field tested at 1.40 mS.Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at 0.8 mS or less.There were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. A rainbow sheen was witnessed in the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and one gas buster staged in secondary containment on the west side of location. While on site the frac tank with the suspected leak and the secondary containment were removed from location. Water puddles adjacent to the frac tank location were vacuumed up. Joe Button discussed that an excavator will be brought to location along with Creston Environmental to conduct cleanup operations at 0800 hrs on 11/17/2022. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b)The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)The department also recommends removing the water from and cleaning the well cellars noted for having sheens; the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with an unknown volume impacting the pad surface.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Violation ID: 976072
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/16/2022
Comments: On 11/16/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. This inspection is in response to Complaint Id 368309 for one barrel of brine water spilled outside of secondary containment from a frac tank on the site.Prior to my arrival, Chesapeake's Danielle Schaad informed me that the frac tank would be to the right when arriving on site and was stationed in secondary containment by itself. She said that the location of the leak in the frac tank and in the secondary containment was unknown but high conductance water was discovered outside of secondary containment on the pad surface. She said that the fluid was brine water from the produced water tank. She reported that the tank and secondary containment had been emptied and the puddle vacuumed up. She said that the tank was being removed from location and that Cresson Environmental would be onsite on 11/17/2022. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours and was melting with the pad being mostly clear of snow. A skid steer and a vac truck had just arrived on location and were setting up next to a frac tank in the northeast corner of the site. The frac tank was still connected to the 1HC gas well GPU. A crew was working on disconnecting it from the GPU. A vac box was located south of the frac tank. I field tested various water puddles in close proximity to the frac tank for conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50 with an upper limit of 20.0 mS with the following results: 40'x 40' water puddle on the south west corner of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 0.77 mS.5' x 8' water puddle outside the southeast corner of the vac box field tested at 14.43 mS.20' x 20' water puddle southeast of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.15 x 30' water puddle east of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.6' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 3.53 mS.12' x 40' water puddle on the east edge of the site above the recently excavated fill slope field tested at 2.33 mS.Water below the rocked section of the fill slope field tested at 1.20 mS. Water in the south end of infiltration area 1 field tested at 1.40 mS.Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at 0.8 mS or less.There were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. A rainbow sheen was witnessed in the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and one gas buster staged in secondary containment on the west side of location. While on site the frac tank with the suspected leak and the secondary containment were removed from location. Water puddles adjacent to the frac tank location were vacuumed up. Joe Button discussed that an excavator will be brought to location along with Creston Environmental to conduct cleanup operations at 0800 hrs on 11/17/2022. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b)The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)The department also recommends removing the water from and cleaning the well cellars noted for having sheens; the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with an unknown volume impacting the pad surface.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: Routine site inspection on May 7, 2026 with DEP representatives Sue Herzing, Justin Galioto, and John Salinkas. The well appears active and capable of producing. Approximately 30 BBL of brine fluids were measured in the 100 BBL brine tank. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, during the inspection and area of exposed soil (~2'x4') was observed to the right of the brine tank (photos 3-4). I screened the exposed soils and elevated readings were observed with 2.01 mS/cm being the highest reading (photos 5-9). A soil sample was collected 3442-976 and sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg and will be tested for SAC 530 plus bromide, lithium, and strontium. While onsite, we contacted Dannic Energy well tender Rob Yohe via phone. Rob was in the area and met us onsite. Rob explained that when he arrived onsite Monday, May 4, 2026, he found that the dump line coming off the well head had corroded off where it connects to top portion of the brine tank and was lying on the ground. The other section remained attached to the well head. He explained that he removed the pipe. He noted, that the well was shut in when he found the dump line lying on the ground. Rob stated that only residual fluids were in the dump line. I explained to Rob, that elevated soils were discovered and that these impacted soils will need to be removed. I contacted Dan Sinclair and left him a voice message regarding my findings. Rob hand excavated impacted soils based off visual impacts to the soil (photos 11-12). I recommended that he cover the excavated area with plastic. The Department recommends screenings the excavated area. Screenings need to be <1.00 mS/cm before being backfilled.Violations have been cited for the brine release. The Department recommends cleaning up spill in accordance with "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads (800-5000-001).

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2021
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 933244
Permit API: 051-23196
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2021
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a complaint received by the Department of corroded production tanks and possible leak. Arrived on-site at approx. 1130 to conduct investigation. Well appeared equipped for production. No well label was observed on any of the production equipment on site. Recommend Operator affix permanent well label IAW the regulations. Well posting was present but has the wrong permit number on posting (Photo 3). Recommend Operator re-post with the appropriate and correct information for this well. Background conductance reading was taken in a field west of well pad (Photo 1). Conductance value in this location was 170 micro Siemens. Heavy corrosion was observed on production tanks. Holes have developed along the south and west sides of tank (Photos 2/4/5/8/9/10). A large hole (2'x2') has developed on the west side of tank. Production fluid/brine observed approx. 3" below large hole (Photo 5). Conductance of liquid in tank was 14,500 micro Siemens (Photo 6). Tank was located within earthen berm. Conductance readings were taken along the ground on the south and south-west sides of tank (Photos 4 & 8). Values were 3,740 & 4,510 micro Siemens respectively. These values were well above the background conductance reading and indicate a release of production fluid/brine onto the ground. Request Operator determine and provide quantity of release, the method how the quantity was determined, and the duration of the release. Recommend the Operator immediately remove all production fluid/brine from the production tank for proper disposal. It is also recommended that this production tank be removed and impacted soils beneath/adjacent to tank be delineated and areas impacted remediated. Production tank should be replaced once remediation is completed and confirmed by both the Operator and Department. NOTE: Conductance readings taken along the earthen berm were at background. It does not appear at this time that the release has migrated laterally. Violations are being cited related to the release of fluids to the ground and well label/posting. Pending Operator's response, additional violations may be cited.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/29/2025 to BRANCH JOHN D in Pleasant Township, Warren county. 78.60(b)2-4 - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Owner or operator land applied tophole water or precipitation water from a pit that is contrary to Department requirements for pH, conductivity and sheen.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BRANCH JOHN D
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/29/2025
Violation Code: 78.60(b)2-4 - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Owner or operator land applied tophole water or precipitation water from a pit that is contrary to Department requirements for pH, conductivity and sheen.
Violation ID: 8250189
Permit API: 123-49050
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/29/2025
Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. I arrived onsite and found a hose running down hill from a tank battery on Farm Lane that was used to hold presumed fresh water during the recent completion of this well. The well operator was draining the water tank and using it to water their freshly seeded and mulched areas. I used my conductivity probe and determined the water being discharged from the tank was not suitable to be dispersed to the ground as the conductance of the fluid was in excess of 16000S, which is above the allowable limit of 1000S. The operator immediately shut the valve and ceased the discharge. It is estimated over 1 barrel of fluid was released prior to closing the valve. Mr. Branch called to get additional equipment onsite to begin remediating the release. It was advised to get a vac truck for any standing water, and the mini excavator on site to begin soil removal.From the end of the discharge hose, the water ran approximately 35 feet in a westerly direction across a portion of the site, reaching an open earthen drainage ditch, this ditch connects to the local storm sewer somewhere along Crestview Blvd. Flowing water in the storm sewer was observed at the bottom of Crestview Blvd, due to lack of access I was unable to get my conductivity probe into the water to determine if it was from the Brown #1 site.

Violation ID: 998674
Permit API: 083-47406
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2023
Comments: This was an inspection performed following a report that the operator had a leaking brine tank on the Enis Lease. I inspected all three tank batteries on this lease.This well is producing and is equipped with a gas powered pumpjack. No spills or leaks are noted at the well. There is a tank battery near the well with two 210 barrel stock tanks contained. There is a buried brine tank across the access road in a wooded area. It appears that there has been an ongoing small leak in the tank, which has allowed brine to leak out into the soil. Impacted soil is apparent ~35 linear feet from the tank, at the base of a small hill. A check with a soil EC meter showed conductivity ranging from 1.5 to 5 mS in the soil. The liquid, along with deer activity, has stripped away vegetation from a 10x15 foot area. The water does not appear to have traveled much further than this and does not appear to be a threat to enter the waters of the Commonwealth.After this visit, I called the operator and he came to the site a little later to look at it with me. He agreed that the tank appeared to be leaking. I suggested that the tank would need to be vacuumed out, removed from the ground and the impacted soils remediated. He said that he would be contacting a contractor immediately to begin this process. Continued followup will be done as necessary.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/23/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8205473
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/23/2024
Comments: On 10/23/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of three water samples that were collected during fracking operations from three different locations at the site. During inspections #3846615 and #3846665, conducted on 10/2/2024 and 10/3/2024; the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. Samples were collected on 10/3/2024. On 10/19/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-142 was collected from the south of two puddles of water near the outfall at the center of the north perimeter berm; both puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductivity on the Altair PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. The south puddle measured 6' x 1.5' x 3 inches and the north puddle measured 10' x 3' x 2". The 16" freshwater pipeline and the 16" frac water pipeline traveled through these puddles. There was a multi-colored crusty sheen and the water left a brown film on the sample bottles. The results are shown in pictures 1-3.Sample 9551-143 was collected from within MRC basin 1 in a water/muddy area where the outfall from the center of the north perimeter berm flows into the basin. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 4-6. Sample 9551-144 was collected from within MRC basin 1, next to the east basin overflow. Water in this area field tested at 1.595 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 7-8.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, manganese, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2). This incident does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b). Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the elevated conductance, aluminum, iron, manganese, strontium and chlorides in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Columbia, Springfield and Troy Townships, Bradford County on 7/16/2025 at 1020 hours. The weather was in the low 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A representative with the DEP's Environmental Cleanups Program and a Repsol representative were present for the inspection. During the DEPs inspection, fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were noted within the secondary constructed berm (photo #2) and within the stormwater control basin (photo #3). Sheet flow of fluids off the edges of the pad surface have subsided. A pump was observed near the stormwater control basin that started recovering fluids held within the basin in the evening hours on 7/15/2025. The DEP continued the monitoring of fluids/soils at set monitoring points in various areas around the well site. Distressed vegetation was observed in areas on the fill slopes (photos #5 and 7) and downslope of the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4). Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were noted downslope of the western corner of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm, which were also noted on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025. A representative with Repsol walked us up to the 7H wellhead. Fluids were observed within the well cellar. As a result of the release, large amounts of sand were observed piled around the wellheads.Repsol is currently working on an estimated volume for the release and has began working on a remediation plan. Resource Environmental (Resource) continues to screen soils to determine surface impacts. At this time, with the exception of the soils off the western corner of the site (near the hedgerow) and along the surface waterline, Resource has not discovered any additional impacted surface soils downslope of the well pad. Repsol plans to construct some sort of stormwater controls downslope of impacted soils to prevent further impacts to the surface.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301.The DEP departed the well site at 1200 hours. For information regarding the DEP's inspections on 7/14/2025 and 7/15/2025, please see inspection record #s 4012602 and 4013600, respectively.

Comments: 10/2/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an administrative inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #4038825, conducted on 8/21/2025, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of thepad. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 1983 uS conductance. Sample 9551-219 was collected from this area. The liquid in the pond next to the northeast overflow weir field tested at 1924 uS conductance. Sample 9551220 was collected from this area.On 9/19/2025, the department received the results of the samples. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.
